name: Kartu Kredit OCBC 90°N

fees.condition: waived after Rp 300.000.000 of transactions in the previous year, for Private Banking customers, for a Premier Banking main card while total combined funds of Rp 500.000.000 are kept, or by redeeming 25.000 Travel Miles for a year

rules.name: Double miles abroad on dining, transport, lodging and airlines

cycleBonuses.name: 1.000 Travel Miles at Rp 60.000.000 a statement

welcomeBonus: 12.000 Travel Miles from 1 February 2026, down from 13.000, for a customer who has not held a Visa 90°N card or closed one more than 3 months ago, with the card activated within 2 months of approval.
notes: Every figure here is from PinterPoin and IndoMiles. Bank OCBC NISP's own site and RIPLAY could not be reached, so nothing is confirmed against the issuer.

The rates changed in November 2025: Rp 10.000 a mile became Rp 12.000 at home and Rp 8.000 became Rp 10.000 abroad. The exact day was not given, so the entry runs the current rates from the start. A cycle before November 2025 is therefore underestimated by about a fifth.

From 13 February 2026 the double miles on foreign-currency dining, transport, lodging and airlines stopped, and so did the 1.000 Travel Miles paid at Rp 60.000.000 a statement. That is the second terms period; cycles before it keep both.

Education, digital advertising and petrol stations stopped earning in November 2025. Education and fuel are matched by category; digital advertising has no category of its own here, so an advertising spend will be overestimated.
Earning is capped at one times the card limit a month, which is read from the card's own terms when the entry is applied, so set the credit limit before relying on the estimate.

The double-miles rule is written as a stackable extra on top of the foreign rate, which doubles it to a mile per Rp 5.000. Whether the bank instead paid a flat doubled rate is not something the sources settle; on whole multiples of Rp 10.000 the two agree.

Redemption is capped at 100.000 Travel Miles a month, down from 150.000 in November 2025, and applied to transfer estimates. Nothing converts past it, and the ceiling covers every partner together, so an estimate showing one airline assumes nothing has gone to the others that month. The drop from 150.000 has no published date, so the entry runs 100.000 throughout.
Travel Miles do not expire and transfers to airline partners carry no fee.

Transfer ratios are quoted relative to KrisFlyer: Asia Miles gives 25% fewer and British Airways and Etihad Guest 10% fewer, which is recorded as 750 and 900 per 1.000 Travel Miles. The real transfer steps and minimums were not published, so 1.000 is a placeholder for the increment.
The annual fee of Rp 1.000.000 can be waived several ways, including redeeming 25.000 Travel Miles for a year. The fee condition records them; the app always shows the fee as charged.
Not the Singapore OCBC 90°N, which is a different card in Singapore dollars earning 1,3 miles per dollar at home and up to 7 through Agoda. Reviews of that card do not describe this one.

A transfer estimate now applies the ceiling. It is spent in whole transfer steps, so a step straddling the ceiling waits for the next window rather than being split, which the issuer's own screens may not do.
